summary: The findings-schema correction is currently OpenAI-strict compatible; no active consumer depends on consumer_payload, and the blind/prompt floor adapters safely tolerate the nullable certification fields. The phase guard is not ready to certify: the sanctioned adapter can omit its binding, the binding is self-attested rather than content-verified, durable git-note evidence is checked only on HEAD, and the purported owner override can be self-authorized by the invoking process.

findings.claim: The retro-plan override is SHA-bound but not authenticated as repository-owner authority.
findings.analysis: parsePhaseOverride trusts an expected digest supplied through the same process environment and an authority string inside the document being approved. A caller capable of launching the review can create the override, compute its digest, set SVC_EXTERNAL_REVIEW_PHASE_OVERRIDE_SHA256 inline, and self-declare authority=repository-owner. The fixture demonstrates exactly this sequence. The digest protects bytes from mutation but does not establish independent owner approval, so an agent can reopen a post-execution plan review itself. Freshness is also weakened by accepting timestamps up to 24 hours in the future via Math.abs, creating an effective replay window approaching 48 hours.
evidence: scripts/run-external-review.mjs:691-708 reads the trust anchor from process.env and validates it against the caller-supplied document.
test-framework/evals/tier-1/validate-external-review-launcher.sh:802-806 creates the override, computes its SHA, and supplies the expected digest inline without an independent owner action.
docs/specs/features/wi-489-reviewer-runtime-routing.md:229 requires a repository-owner, SHA-pinned, fresh override as the sole exception.
docs/specs/decisions/wi-489-reviewer-runtime-routing.md:79-85 separately recognizes environment-variable overrides as ephemeral and weakly auditable.
findings.proposed_fix: Authorize retro-plan review through an independently established owner approval that the reviewing process cannot mint, such as a signed approval record or protected supervisor-provided token. Bind the approval to WI, plan hash, base commit, and expiry. Reject timestamps later than a small clock-skew allowance and older than the configured lifetime.

findings.claim: The sanctioned review-plan adapter does not always supply a phase binding and can silently restore the original unguarded paid-plan path.
findings.analysis: When neither the branch nor plan text yields an uppercase WI-N identifier, the adapter warns and invokes the launcher without --phase-binding. Because phase binding is optional by default for backward compatibility, that invocation can reach the provider even after execution began. This directly contradicts EXTREV-136's requirement that the sanctioned adapter always supplies the binding. Selecting the first WI occurrence from free-form plan text can also bind a dependency WI instead of the reviewed WI.
evidence: scripts/review-plan-codex.sh:37-49 derives WI using first-match grep and explicitly proceeds without a binding on failure.
scripts/review-plan-codex.sh:77 still invokes the paid launcher when PHASE_ARGS is empty.
scripts/run-external-review.mjs:1271-1277 allows a missing binding unless SVC_EXTERNAL_REVIEW_REQUIRE_PHASE_BINDING=1 is set.
docs/specs/features/wi-489-reviewer-runtime-routing.md:224 says the sanctioned adapter always supplies the binding.
The adapter fixture at test-framework/evals/tier-1/validate-external-review-launcher.sh:714-734 covers only a branch containing an unambiguous WI identifier.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the adapter fail before launcher invocation unless it can derive exactly one authoritative WI. Prefer structured manifest or task-graph metadata over free-text grep, reject ambiguity, and always pass --phase-binding. Add detached-HEAD, missing-WI, and multiple-WI fixtures proving zero provider calls.

findings.claim: Durable exec-record lookup can miss authoritative receipts attached to an ancestor commit.
findings.analysis: The framework contract defines git notes as authoritative and the working-tree receipt mirror as a regenerable cache. findExecRecordForWi searches the cache, then checks only the note attached to HEAD. If the mirror is absent and HEAD has advanced after the execution commit, an exec-record on an ancestor is ignored. With no remaining implementation divergence—for example after a revert or an execution that only produced exempt paths—the plan review is allowed despite durable execution evidence existing for the WI.
evidence: references/chain-receipt-contract.md:7-14 defines refs/notes/svc-receipts as durable authority and .svc/receipts as a regenerable cache.
references/chain-receipt-contract.md:103-107 says validation reads git notes authoritatively and regenerates a missing mirror.
scripts/run-external-review.mjs:622-656 scans the mirror and then runs git notes show HEAD only.
test-framework/evals/tier-1/validate-external-review-launcher.sh:786-798 tests only a working-tree staging mirror, not an authoritative note on a non-HEAD ancestor.
docs/specs/features/wi-489-reviewer-runtime-routing.md:225-227 requires any durable exec-record for the WI to block the plan review.
findings.proposed_fix: Search authoritative notes for the relevant commit range or reuse receipt-validation code that resolves the WI's durable receipt history, rather than inspecting HEAD alone. Add a fixture with an exec-record note on an ancestor, a later exempt-only commit, no mirror, and zero implementation delta; the review must reject before spawn.

findings.claim: The phase binding does not cryptographically or mechanically bind the reviewed plan or the true pre-execution state.
findings.analysis: plan_manifest_sha256 is optional, format-checked only, and never compared with the actual plan content. The caller also chooses contextRoot and pre_execution_base at review time. A direct caller can therefore bind WI-X to the current post-execution HEAD, omit or invent the plan hash, and make implementationDivergedFromBase report no changes. SVC_EXTERNAL_REVIEW_REQUIRE_PHASE_BINDING=1 checks only that a binding file exists, not that it originated before execution or matches the reviewed plan. The sanctioned adapter normally supplies merge-base and a real hash, but the canonical launcher itself accepts an untrusted self-attestation.
evidence: scripts/run-external-review.mjs:677-688 permits plan_manifest_sha256 to be absent and validates only its syntax when present.
scripts/run-external-review.mjs:711-745 records plan_manifest_sha256 but never verifies it against package or filesystem content.
scripts/run-external-review.mjs:1157-1163 accepts caller-selected contextRoot.
scripts/run-external-review.mjs:659-674 compares against the caller-supplied base without establishing when that base was captured.

test-framework/evals/tier-1/validate-external-review-launcher.sh:756-765 calls the guarded plan path with a binding that omits plan_manifest_sha256, so the missing content binding is treated as a successful fixture.
docs/specs/features/wi-489-reviewer-runtime-routing.md:224 requires the binding to include WI identity, pre-execution base, and plan-manifest hash.
findings.proposed_fix: Create the phase binding when the plan-manifest receipt is emitted and store it in authoritative receipt state. At review time, resolve WI, base, plan path, and plan hash from that durable record; recompute the plan hash and reject mismatch. Require plan_manifest_sha256 in parsePhaseBinding and add fixtures for missing hash, forged hash, post-execution HEAD as base, and mismatched context root.
